recommendations.text: Verbal de-escalation should always be attempted before pharmacological or physical interventions.

For Agitation Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - assess safety of environment (within 2 minutes) - attempt verbal deescalation (within 10 minutes) - assess medical causes - obtain vital signs - check glucose (within 10 minutes)
During Agitation Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: restrain without attempting deescalation, leave patient unsupervised while agitated.
Medication choice depends on suspected etiology, comorbidities, and contraindications.
For Pharmacologic Intervention, the following actions are mandatory: - choose appropriate medication (within 15 minutes) - monitor sedation level - monitor respiratory status (within 20 minutes)

Alcohol + high-dose benzodiazepine causes profound respiratory depression. Use antipsychotic (haloperidol, olanzapine) instead or low-dose benzo with close monitoring.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_benzodiazepine_high_dose, give_lorazepam_4mg, give_midazolam_10mg] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: BETA Project 2012; Nobay F, Ann Emerg Med 2004

recommendations.text:
QTc > 500ms + haloperidol causes Torsades de Pointes and sudden cardiac death. Use benzodiazepine (lorazepam) or olanzapine instead.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_haloperidol, give_droperidol] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: FDA Black Box Warning - haloperidol QT prolongation; APA 2024

recommendations.text:
Typical antipsychotics in Parkinson/LBD cause severe neuroleptic sensitivity reaction, irreversible parkinsonism, NMS. Use low-dose quetiapine if needed.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_haloperidol, give_droperidol, give_chlorpromazine] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: APA 2024; McKeith IG, Neurology 2005 - neuroleptic sensitivity in LBD

recommendations.text:
IM olanzapine + IM benzodiazepine causes respiratory arrest (multiple case reports). FDA contraindication. Wait adequate time between agents or use different combination.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_lorazepam_im, give_benzodiazepine_im] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: Olanzapine IM package insert; FDA warning - respiratory depression with IM benzo combo

recommendations.text: Physical restraint is last resort. Prone and hobble restraints are prohibited due to positional asphyxia risk.

For Physical Restraint, the following actions are mandatory: - apply least restrictive restraint - monitor neurovascular status q15min (within 15 minutes) - document restraint indication (within 15 minutes) - reassess need q1h
During Physical Restraint, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: prone restraint, hobble restraint, leave restrained patient unmonitored.
Immediate cessation of offending agent, aggressive cooling, and IV hydration are critical first steps.

For NMS / Serotonin Syndrome Recognition, the following actions are mandatory: - stop offending agent (within 5 minutes) - aggressive cooling (within 5 minutes) - give iv fluids - monitor ck renal function

NMS requires immediate dantrolene (direct muscle relaxant) and cessation of all antipsychotics. Mortality is 10-20% without treatment.
 [REQUIRED: give_dantrolene, stop_all_antipsychotics] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: APA 2024 NMS Guidelines; Strawn JR, CNS Drugs 2007

recommendations.text: NMS is caused by dopamine blockade from antipsychotics; readministering any antipsychotic worsens the syndrome fatally. [FORBIDDEN: give_antipsychotic_in_nms, give_haloperidol_in_nms] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: APA Practice Guidelines; NMS is caused by antipsychotic dopamine blockade; readministering antipsychotics is fatal

recommendations.text:
Serotonin syndrome requires cyproheptadine (5-HT2A antagonist) and cessation of all serotonergic agents. Distinguish from NMS by clonus, hyperreflexia, and diarrhea (absent in NMS).
 [REQUIRED: give_cyproheptadine, stop_serotonergic_agents] (Severity: CRITICAL)

SSRIs and tramadol increase serotonin further in serotonin syndrome; all serotonergic agents must be discontinued. [FORBIDDEN: give_ssri_in_serotonin_syndrome, give_tramadol_in_serotonin_syndrome] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: APA Practice Guidelines; Boyer EW, NEJM 2005; serotonergic agents compound serotonin syndrome
